name: Fuel dispenser and underground tank

comps.spec: Petrol and diesel in underground tanks, often tens of thousands of litres — reach it through the fill or gauge port with a hand pump; vapours ignite easily, so no sparks or electric pumps
comps.loc: Underground tanks; fill caps under flush covers in the forecourt

comps.spec: Fuel-rated rubber hoses, 3–5 m, with nozzles and breakaway couplings
comps.loc: On each side of the dispenser

comps.spec: Submersible turbine fuel pump, about 0.5–1.5 kW mains, in the tank

comps.loc: Hydraulic cabinet, on top of each meter

notes: With the grid down the pumps are dead, so the fuel stays in the ground. Petrol goes stale within months; diesel keeps longer. Check for water at the bottom of the tank.
